summary:
AgroShift is a web-based agronomic decision-support tool that helps farmers and technicians plan crop rotations and protect soil health under changing climate conditions, without requiring field sensors.

Users search any location and pinpoint their field—or trace its perimeter in hectares—on an interactive satellite map. AgroShift then retrieves real-time NASA POWER climate and soil moisture series, 5-year historical trends, MODIS NDVI (MOD13Q1) vegetation vigor, and terrain slope to diagnose water deficit, reference evaporation (Eo), heat stress, and erosion risk. Next, users can test the local viability of any crop or cover species and instantly export a Technical Parcel Dossier in PDF with actionable rotation recommendations.

This matters because it turns complex Earth observation data into clear, free, multilingual guidance to prevent soil degradation and improve climate resilience for small and medium-scale growers.
details:
What it does & how it works AgroShift is a web application that guides farmers, agronomists, and cooperatives through a 4-step field workflow:

Global Parcel Selection: Users search any country, region, or town (via Open-Meteo Geocoding) and either click a point or trace their field's perimeter on an interactive Leaflet satellite map. AgroShift computes the geodesic area in hectares (ha), perimeter length, and centroid in real time.

Earth Observation Diagnostics: For the selected parcel, the backend fetches the last 30 days of daily agroclimatology (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, RH2M, PRECTOTCORR, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, WS2M) and 5-year monthly trends (T2M, PRECTOTCORR, GWETTOP, GWETROOT) from NASA POWER, plus MODIS MOD13Q1 250 m 16-day NDVI vegetation composites from ORNL DAAC and terrain elevation/slope from Open-Meteo. Using Penman (1948) / RELASPO reference evaporation (Eo), FAO-56, and RUSLE slope risk criteria, it diagnoses water balance, heat/frost stress, soil moisture shifts, and erosion risk.

Current Crop & Dynamic Plant Viability: Users select what is currently growing (cereal, tuber, legume, or perennial orchard/vineyard) to see rotation problems and solutions—avoiding incompatible recommendations like tall cereals inside perennial orchards—and can evaluate any plant species dynamically against local NASA climate data using FAO EcoCrop thresholds and Wikipedia botanical metadata.

Technical Parcel Dossier & PDF Export: AgroShift synthesizes water status, soil alerts, and top crop/cover rotation options into an on-screen dossier and a formatted, downloadable PDF field report (jsPDF).

Benefits & intended impact

Zero-hardware accessibility: Runs in any desktop or mobile browser with no IoT sensors, helping small and medium-scale growers make science-backed planting decisions for free.

Soil & water conservation: Encourages nitrogen-fixing legumes, low-water crops, and living cover crops between orchard rows to curb evaporation, reduce fertilizer dependency, and prevent soil degradation.

Intended impact: Reduce crop failure caused by shifting rainfall and heat patterns while promoting sustainable crop rotation habits across diverse agricultural regions, available in four languages (English, Spanish, French, and Portuguese).

Tools, languages, hardware & software

Languages & Frameworks: TypeScript 5, Next.js 16.3.4 (App Router), React 19.2.8, Tailwind CSS 4.

Mapping & PDF: Leaflet 1.9.4 (Esri World Imagery with automatic OpenStreetMap fallback), custom spherical geodesic area/Haversine utilities, Lucide React, and jsPDF for client-side PDF generation.

APIs & Services: NASA POWER API, NASA ORNL DAAC MODIS API, Open-Meteo (Geocoding, Elevation, Soil Moisture Forecast), Meteomatics (optional 7-day forecast), Wikipedia REST API, and Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (with deterministic rule-based fallback).

Development Hardware/Software: Standard developer laptops, Node.js, Git, and GitHub.

Creativity Instead of showing raw satellite charts that require technical training, AgroShift combines interactive geodesic perimeter drawing directly on satellite imagery with an open-ended plant feasibility checker and an actionable PDF dossier tailored to whether the field grows annual crops or permanent orchards. It bridges hydro-agronomic models (Penman 1948 / RELASPO, FAO-56, RUSLE) with accessible, farmer-friendly UX.

Factors our team considered

Perennial vs. annual crop logic: Perennial orchards (e.g., grapes, fruit trees) cannot be uprooted for annual rotation, so the system recommends low-stature cover crops for inter-row alleys instead of tall cereals.

Satellite & pixel limitations: Coarse 250 m NDVI pixels mix soil and canopy in small plots, so NDVI is paired with local climate, Eo, and terrain slope rather than used in isolation.

Resilience & reliability: Slow external APIs (such as MODIS) load asynchronously without blocking core climate diagnostics, and AI-assisted features gracefully fall back to deterministic agronomic calculations if API quotas are unavailable.

Multilingual & field usability: Full EN/ES/FR/PT localization and offline-ready printable/PDF dossiers for use in rural areas with limited connectivity.
